sentences.text:
The present petition is filed by the petitioner seeking direction to respondent No.2-Special Land Acquisition Officer to pass general award in respect of the land bearing Sy.No.32/2, New No.70,
measuring 0.30 guntas of Haraluru Village, Channarayapatna Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and to deposit the award amount before the jurisdictional Civil Court.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had earlier filed a civil suit in O.S.No.221/2020 against respondent No.3 and the said suit has been dismissed and as against the same, he has filed the miscellaneous petition.
He further submits that, an appeal has been filed before the Deputy Commissioner and the same is also pending consideration.
3. Learned counsel for the KIADB on instructions submits that, award had already been passed and the compensation amount has also been disbursed.

In that view of NC: 2025:KHC:201 the matter,
the relief sought for in the writ petition has become infructuous.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner does not dispute the same.
However, he submits that notwithstanding the award having been passed and the same having been disbursed, the petitioner be granted liberty to seek such remedy as may be available under law.
5. Submission is taken on record.
Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of as having become infructuous with liberty as sought for.

SD/-
(M.G.S. KAMAL) JUDGE PK Sri Muniyappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45426157/
